big_idea: BLEND sounds smoothly to read a word: /c/-/a/-/t/ slides into CAT.
learning_intention: We are learning to blend sounds to decode CVC words.
student_learning_goal: I can blend sounds to decode CVC words.
success_criteria: I can SAY each sound in a CVC word.
I can SLIDE the sounds together smoothly.
I can READ the blended word.
I can BLEND a word I have not seen before.
lesson_specific_materials: 3-Box Sound Box Cards (drawn with marker on index cards)
Letter index cards (lowercase a-z; 1 set per pair)
10 CVC word slips (written on index card halves; 5 known + 5 new)

minds_on.hook: Sounder + Blendy: /c/... /a/... /t/... CAT! When sounds SLIDE together, that's BLENDING.
minds_on.teacher_script:
Both characters at the carpet. 'Reader friends — Sounder taught us SOUNDS. Blendy taught us LETTERS make sounds. Today we learn to BLEND — slide sounds together to read a whole word.'

Define. 'BLEND means slide sounds together smoothly: /c/-/a/-/t/ → CAT. Same sounds, faster, no pauses.'

Demo with hand gestures. Hold up three fingers. 'First sound: /c/.' Touch finger 1. '/c/-/c/-/c/.' 'Middle sound: /a/.' Touch finger 2. '/a/-/a/-/a/.' 'Last sound: /t/.' Touch finger 3. '/t/-/t/-/t/.' Slide hand across all three. '/c/-/a/-/t/. CAT!'

Class repeats with hand gesture. CAT, MAT, SUN.

Map and blend on the front sound box. Place letter cards C-A-T. Point to each letter and say its sound: /c/, /a/, /t/. Then sweep finger left to right under the boxes: /c/-/a/-/t/ → CAT.

'Blendy says — point to each letter, say its sound, then SLIDE.'

Demo with three more known words: D-O-G → DOG, P-I-N → PIN, M-A-P → MAP.

Now blend a NEW word the children have not seen. Build L-I-D in the front sound box. Class points and sounds: /l/-/i/-/d/. Slide. 'LID! That is a word — a top for a pot!'

One more new word. Build B-U-S. /b/-/u/-/s/. Slide. 'BUS!'

'Sounder + Blendy say — the magic is the SLIDE. Each sound, then slide them together!'
student_actions: Watch Sounder and Blendy demo blend gesture
Echo CAT, MAT, SUN with hand slide
Read DOG, PIN, MAP from front sound box
Blend LID and BUS — new words

steps.instruction: Hand each pair a Sound Box Card, a Letter Card set, and 10 word slips.
For each word slip, pairs build the word with letter cards in the sound boxes, then point and sound each letter, then slide to read.
Pairs alternate: one builds, one reads, then swap.
Last 5 word slips are NEW words. Encourage independent blending.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say: 'New words — blend on your own.'
Stop at each pair. Listen for smooth slide, not letter-by-letter pause.

differentiation.for_emerging: Use 5 word slips only, all known. Teacher slides hand under the letters as a model.
differentiation.for_extending: Pairs change one letter to make a new word: PIG → BIG → BIT.
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Pre-build the first letter; child completes the rest.
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Stand, slide hand from shoulder to fingertip while saying the blend.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Five signals: builds word; sounds each letter; slides smoothly without pause; reads the whole word; transfers to new words.

discussion_prompts: Show the blend gesture for CAT.
What new word did you read today?
Why do we slide sounds together?
consolidation.exit_routine: Each child blends ONE new word out loud: '/__/-/__/-/__/, that's ___!' Class chants 'HOO knows the sounds? YOU do!'

assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 3 captures B2.2 (continued) and B2.3 (decoding) — blending is the bridge.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child PAUSES between sounds and cannot blend — repairing the choppy-blend trap at Grade 1
expanded_walkthrough.rationale: Common Grade-1 trap on B2.3: child says '/c/ ... /a/ ... /t/' with long pauses between sounds, then can't say the word. Without continuous airflow the phonemes don't fuse — children hear 3 separate sounds, not a word. This is a fluency-of-blending issue, distinct from segmenting.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Blend activity. Child reads C-A-T as '/c/ ... /a/ ... /t/. ... /c/ ... /a/ ... /t/. ... I don't know.'
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Blendy asks — slide the sounds. No stops between.'

Probe. 'Like this: /c/-/a/-/t/. No pause. Try with me.' Demonstrate, then do it together.

Generalise. 'Blendy says — when you slide sounds with no pause, your mouth almost says the word. Faster, smoother, no stop.'

If still choppy: hold the first sound. '/cccccc-aaaaaaa-t/.' The continuous airflow forces fusion. Then ask the child to copy.

If the child has a clear-but-slow blend, that is OK at Grade 1; smoothness comes with practice. The trap is total fragmentation with no fusion.
expected_student_responses: (Mid) '/c/-/a/-/t/' with prompts, then 'CAT' after teacher models
(Stretched) Blends a 4-letter word like PLAN with the same gesture
common_misconceptions: Slow is fine. (Repair: pauses break blend; smooth is the goal.)
I don't know means stop. (Repair: try sliding faster.)
recovery_moves: Slide hand left-to-right under the letters as the child says it.
Compare a known word (CAT, smooth) to the new word so the gesture is identical.
If still stuck after two attempts, return to two sounds first: '/c/-/a/' → 'ca'. Add the third when blending two is fluent.

worksheet_brief.purpose: Independent practice of blending CVC words.

parts_outline.task: Sound-by-sound: 4 sound-box words with letters already placed. Sound each letter and read the word.
Match word to picture: 4 sound-box words on the left, 4 pictures on the right. Read each word and draw a line to its picture.
Read a new word: 2 sound-box words the child has not seen before. Read and write the word on the line below.
